stories.notes: Story has empty acceptance criteria and no existing spec. Title implies a complex multi-platform (GO, UP, MX) live preview feature requiring requirement elaboration first, then testability and security hardening. Assigning both agents with openspec first to define ACs and technical depth, followed by speckit for edge cases and security review.

agentContributions.notes: Novel capability — Live Preview does not exist in the codebase. The central integration point is useContent (236+ callers), which all Contentstack components consume. Live preview must plug into this hook so every consumer receives real-time CMS updates without individual changes. Contentstack external services are unreachable at test time; criteria stop at our side of the boundary.

Openspec provided zero acceptance criteria, so all 14 ACs are new. I built on openspec's architectural note that useContent (236+ callers) is the central integration point and that Contentstack services are unreachable at test time. ACs are written as observable outcomes stopping at our side of the boundary. Key design decisions: (1) AC-1 sets a 2-second SLA for update delivery; (2) AC-3 and AC-4 cover error boundaries since network unreliability is the norm; (3) AC-5, AC-6, AC-14 cover subscription lifecycle to prevent memory leaks; (4) AC-10 addresses rapid-update throttling to prevent performance degradation; (5) AC-11 ensures surgical re-renders so 236+ consumers don't all re-render on every update; (6) AC-13 addresses security — Live Preview tokens/IDs must not leak. CAVEAT: I do not have the file contents for useContent.ts, contentstack.ts, or the three component files. My ACs are inferred from paths, the story title, and openspec's note. If useContent already has partial Live Preview support, some ACs may need adjustment once file contents are available.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: OpenSpec identified the key integration point (useContent, 236+ callers) and the test-time boundary constraint, providing useful architectural context. However, for a story with empty acceptance criteria, OpenSpec's primary responsibility was AC elaboration and it produced zero ACs — a significant under-delivery on its core mandate. SpecKit compensated by generating 14 well-structured ACs covering SLA, error boundaries, subscription lifecycle, throttling, re-render scope, and security token leakage. The value is non-overlapping: OpenSpec provided architectural framing, SpecKit built the testable criteria on top of it. The critical risk is that SpecKit explicitly states it never read useContent.ts, contentstack.ts, or the component files — all 14 ACs are inferred from paths, the title, and OpenSpec's note. If useContent already has partial Live Preview support, some ACs may be redundant or misaligned. A human must verify the ACs against the actual codebase before implementation proceeds.
